To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the right ventricle (RV) is a complex, three-dimensional (3D) structure that is difficult to assess with echocardiography (echo), but can be accurately assessed by cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMR) in both healthy individuals and in patients with heart disease.

(1) the use of a single measurement of the RV diameter is a poor method to assess RV size; (2) the use of the RV diameter to assess RV function is even more inaccurate; and (3) the use of RV fractional area change (RVFAC) is a more accurate measure of RV size and function than RV diameters.
the use of MRI is more accurate than echocardiography for the measurement of right ventricular (RV) size and function.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new method for the assessment of right ventricular (RV) size and function.
the study of the right ventricle (RV) and the RV function in patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH).
the development of novel, high-resolution, non-invasive imaging techniques for the diagnosis of cardiac diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MRI is a more accurate and reproducible technique than echocardiography for the assessment of right ventricular volumes and function.
MRI is the best imaging modality for the assessment of right ventricle size and function, but echo has its own role and should not be abandoned.
echocardiographic evaluation of right ventricular function is feasible, reproducible, and clinically relevant, but that it is limited in its ability to provide quantitative information.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to demonstrate that the RV size and function can be accurately assessed by echocardiography, which is a widely used and easily available tool in the clinical practice.
we have demonstrated that echo is a reliable and accurate tool for the assessment of right ventricular (RV) size and function in children.
the echocardiographic and MRI measurements of right ventricular (RV) size and function are highly correlated and have a similar prognostic value.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the RV is a dynamic organ and that its size and function are not static.

we have demonstrated that a novel, non-contrast magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) technique, known as balanced steady-state free precession, can be used to measure the size of the right ventricle (RV) and its function.
there is a need for a standardized approach to the assessment of right ventricular (RV) size and function, as well as a need to standardize the reporting of these parameters.
